Commanders' Clock Management Mistake Raises Concerns

Washington's loss to San Francisco followed another costly mistake against the New York Giants in Week 5.

During overtime of a 27-27 tie, Daniels scrambled with 12 seconds remaining and no timeouts, allowing the clock to expire before Washington could attempt a game-winning field goal.

Wilson connected that missed opportunity to the Commanders' latest defeat. Washington lost 23-17 to the 49ers, and the points left on the field became especially important as the game progressed.

Wilson noted that Washington later failed to convert another fourth-and-8 attempt after taking a sack. Had the Commanders secured points from their earlier opportunities, they could have put themselves in position to win after getting the ball back late.

"They did a great job coming back," Wilson said, crediting Washington's fight despite the mistakes.

With consecutive games exposing similar problems, Washington, which ranks 20th in PFN NFL Offense Impact %20assigns,red%20zone%20and%20third%20downs.), cannot afford another costly breakdown in game management.

articles.title: Grading Every Cleveland Browns Position Group Entering Week 7
articles.summary: Sitting at 4-2 through six weeks, the Cleveland Browns have a lot to be happy about and plenty to celebrate.
articles.body:
Sitting at 4-2 through six weeks, the Cleveland Browns have a lot to be happy about and plenty to celebrate.

But like any good group project in school, not everyone deserves the same amount of credit.

Some have helped the cause. Some have hindered it.

Let's take a look at whose contributions have helped establish a playoff contender and whose have held the team back despite a strong start.

Key Contributors: Deshaun Watson (111-of-174, 1,174 yards, seven touchdowns, two interceptions, 43.6 QBR)

Demonstrated Strengths: Watson has come through when it matters most. He has orchestrated three fourth-quarter comebacks and four game-winning drives, leading the league in both categories.

He's mostly kept the ball out of harm's way with only two interceptions. That has given them a chance to close out some games in the final quarter.

Needs Improvement: The rest of the game. Despite the 4-2 record and plays in the clutch, he has also posted a negative EPA per dropback through six weeks. Watson's inconsistencies in pocket management have played a role in him taking 24 sacks already.

Key Contributor: Quinshon Judkins (73 carries, 221 yards, one rushing touchdown, 18 receptions, 102 yards)

Demonstrated Strengths: Not many. Judkins is averaging three yards per carry and his longest run of the season was 14 yards. The best we can say at this point is that he hasn't had a fumble this season. Jaleel McLaughlin was serviceable as the lead back with Judkins out in Week 6.

Needs Improvement: Explosive plays. The Browns have four runs of at least 20 yards this season. Deshaun Watson accounts for three of them, all on scrambles—effectively an extension of the passing game. Jaleel McLaughlin has the only other such run.

The offensive line bears some responsibility, but the Browns have to either get more out of their run schemes or find help at the position.

Key Contributors: Denzel Boston (17 catches, 345 yards, three touchdowns), KC Concepcion (22 catches, 186 yards), Jerry Jeudy (12 catches, 150 yards)

Demonstrated Strengths: Denzel Boston has flashed the potential to be a legitimate big-play NFL receiver. He currently leads the league in yards per reception (20.3).

Concepcion has yet to break out, but he's generally catching what's thrown his way. Jeudy has made some clutch catches over the last few weeks.

Needs Improvement: The group needs more consistency across the board. Boston has put up some big games, but he just had one catch for 15 yards on five targets last week.

Concepcion has been schemed a lot of touches, but has just two receptions of more than 20 yards.

A consistent third receiver would be helpful. Jeudy has shown up in high-leverage situations a few times, but he's been invisible for full games in Weeks 2, 3 and 5. Isaiah Bond hasn't stepped up when called on either.

Key Contributors: Harold Fannin Jr. (19 catches, 166 yards, three touchdowns)

Demonstrated Strengths: The statline doesn't show it, but Fannin is getting open. He has the third-highest average separation score among tight ends this season. He's also one of the Browns' top red-zone receiving threats with three touchdowns on the season.

Needs Improvement: Overall, Fannin just hasn't been as involved in the pass game as he should be. He has just five catches for 40 yards over the last three games.

Blake Whiteheart had a few targets early in the season, but his production has completely dried up. At this point, the best thing the tight ends could do is help in the run game, but their blocking has not stood out.

Key Contributors: Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, Austin Barber, Tytus Howard

Demonstrated Strengths: Zion Johnson struggled in the first few weeks, but he has turned out to be a strong addition at left guard. He has yet to give up a sack this year. Austin Barber and Spencer Fano have each put together performances that have shown they can play in the league.

Needs Improvement: As a unit, things have been rough. The Browns are 26th in yards before contact per rush. They're 27th in pressure rate allowed and have given up more sacks than anyone in the league (24).

Some of those pass rush issues can be pinned on Watson. However, the unit has given up pressure with porous blitz pickups and flat-out losing one-on-one pass blocking situations.

Key Contributors: Mason Graham (four sacks), Jared Verse (25 run stops), Isaiah McGuire (23 run stops, three sacks), Maliek Collins (3.5 sacks)

Demonstrated Strengths: Thus far, the Browns have been able to replace Myles Garrett's production in the aggregate. Mason Graham has been out the last two weeks, but had several splash plays before suffering a knee injury.

Jared Verse might not be putting up the pass-rushing numbers most would like to see, but he's been an elite edge-setter in the run game. He's third in the league in run stop win rate among all edges.

Overall, the Browns have put together a defensive front that seems to have quarterbacks on their back foot and does well enough defending the run with their edge-rushers.

Needs Improvement: Health. The production along the defensive line speaks for itself at this point. The Browns' ability to get after the passer with the front four while mixing in some blitzes is driving the defense.

The only problem is that Mason Graham, Mike Hall Jr., Maliek Collins and Derek Barnett are all on the injury report. They need to get as much of their depth on the field as possible to carry this level of play throughout the season.

Key Contributors: Carson Schwesinger (56 tackles, three TFL, one sack, two forced fumbles), Quincy Williams (40 tackles, three tackles for loss, two passes defended and three forced fumbles)

Demonstrated Strengths: The linebacker duo of Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams is one of the best in the league right now. Schwesinger has proven to be one of the fastest-closing linebackers in the league and Williams is a perfect old-school thumper to play beside him.

Needs Improvement: For all of the impressive things that Schwesinger does to stop the run game from sideline to sideline, he is leaving meat on the bone in the coverage game.

Through six games, he's been targeted 22 times, giving up a passer rating of 119.7 with two touchdowns.

Key Contributors: Denzel Ward (25 tackles, one INT, three PD), Grant Delpit (25 tackles, one INT, three PD), Tyson Campbell (25 tackles, one TFL, two PD), Emmanuel McNeil-Warren (24 tackles, three passes defended)

Demonstrated Strengths: Denzel Ward is still playing just about as well as ever. He has given up just 126 yards in coverage for the season thus far. Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has already flashed elite potential and actually has the third-highest PFF grade among all safeties scored this season.

Only two receivers have topped 100 receiving yards in a game against Cleveland this season: DK Metcalf and Garrett Wilson.

Needs Improvement: Forcing turnovers. The Browns have just four interceptions and that's why they are just 16th in passer rating allowed . Covering receivers and tight ends in the slot has been particularly difficult. Myles Harden has been up-and-down throughout the season and Ronnie Hickman leads the team in missed tackles.

articles.title: Grading Every Buffalo Bills Position Group at the Week 7 Bye
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills have hit their bye as the lone one-loss team in the NFL.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have hit their bye as the lone one-loss team in the NFL.

That leaves only the league's three remaining unbeaten teams—the San Francisco 49ers, Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs—with better records than the 5-1 Bills.

Which position groups are most responsible for the strong start? Which groups have held the squad back as they've made a habit of surviving rather than thriving? Let's break it down with group-by-group grades as the team takes a Week 7 breather.

Demonstrated Strengths: He's the CEO of the league's highest-scoring offense, having navigated the team to a 5-1 start despite being hampered by a banged-up receiving corps and a defense that has given him no margin for error. Allen ranks second among qualified passers with 8.8 yards per attempt, and he leads the entire NFL with eight rushing touchdowns in six games.

Needs Improvement: Only four quarterbacks have committed more turnover-worthy plays than Allen (11), and he's somewhat lucky he has thrown just four interceptions. Allen's tendency to play hero and carry the team on his shoulders can be a double-edged sword, and on several occasions he'd have been better off taking the more conservative approach.

Personnel: James Cook, Ty Johnson, Ray Davis

Demonstrated Strengths: Cook is the league's third-leading rusher, also ranking in the top five with a yards-per-attempt average of 5.4. Meanwhile, Johnson and Davis have provided effective relief with 213 scrimmage yards on just 22 touches. This unit boasts both a workhorse star and reliable depth.

Needs Improvement: The only problem is Cook has fumbled four times, bringing that total to a ridiculous nine in his last 15 outings.

Personnel: DJ Moore, Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Joshua Palmer, Skyler Bell

Demonstrated Strengths: Moore has been productive when healthy, while Coleman has stepped up in a major way with three high-volume performances. He's experiencing a breakout third season, while Shakir has had some strong moments in an otherwise bleh campaign to date.

Needs Improvement: Moore has been on the field for just 34 percent of the team's offensive snaps this season, so the improvements have to start with his bum shoulder. Beyond that, they may eventually need Palmer or Bell to actually do something. Neither has been reliable, which is particularly unfortunate considering that Palmer's making $10 million a year.

Personnel: Dalton Kincaid, Dawson Knox, Jackson Hawes

Demonstrated Strengths: Only Travis Kelce (15.0) is averaging more yards per catch at the tight end position than Kincaid (13.7). The 2023 first-round pick has been a huge factor in three Buffalo wins, while Knox adds receiving depth and Hawes provides pure blocking value.

Needs Improvement: Both Kincaid and Knox have a tendency to disappear. The former caught a combined four passes in a three-game stretch earlier this fall, while Knox has yet to put up 15 receiving yards in a game.

Personnel: Dion Dawkins, Alec Anderson, Connor McGovern, O'Cyrus Torrence, Spencer Brown

Demonstrated Strengths: The unit has excelled at opening up running lanes all season for a team that is averaging 5.1 yards per carry. Cook leads the NFL in yards per attempt before contact, and Allen is one of eight qualified quarterbacks with a pressure rate below 20 percent. There's a lot of continuity here, and this group has tremendous intuition when it comes to working with Allen as he maneuvers the pocket.

Needs Improvement: Pro Football Focus actually ranks this line in the bottom 10 in terms of pass-blocking efficiency. The 32-year-old Dawkins appears to be in decline, and penalties have become a significant problem on the left side, particularly as Anderson continues to get up to speed as a starter.

Personnel: Ed Oliver, T.J. Sanders, Deone Walker, DeWayne Carter, Greg Gaines, Landon Jackson

Demonstrated Strengths: This multi-dimensional front is the main reason why the Bills have surrendered just one 20-yard run all season. Deone Walker is absolutely killing it in both run and pass defense and is easily on track to put together his first Pro Bowl campaign at age 22. Carter, Gaines and Jackson are superb depth guys with playmaking ability, and Oliver and Sanders are above-average starters when healthy.

Needs Improvement: The concern is availability: Oliver and Sanders have already missed a combined seven games, leaving a lot on the shoulders of guys they'd prefer to play situationally.

Personnel: Bradley Chubb, Greg Rousseau, Michael Hoecht

Demonstrated Strengths: Rousseau leads the league with 19 quarterback hits and has been a huge factor across the board with six sacks, solid run defense and even tremendous pass coverage in a new role as part of Jim Leonhard's 3-4-oriented defense.

Needs Improvement: The supporting cast needs to contribute more, and the unit's sack production has dropped off recently. Rousseau's six sacks came in the first three weeks, and the three edge-defenders listed here have a combined zero sacks in the last three weeks. Chubb hasn't been as ineffective as the raw numbers indicate, but a total of 1.5 sacks and 10 pressures in six games is not adequate.

Personnel: Terrel Bernard, Dorian Williams

Demonstrated Strengths: Bernard functions primarily as a cleanup artist who regularly reads and diagnoses plays correctly but often struggles to execute. Williams gets off blocks better than Bernard and is a decent run defender overall, though he has struggled in coverage and with open-field tackling.

Needs Improvement: Over the last six weeks, this has been the roster's least reliable position group. Bernard and Williams have struggled with execution and tackling as an off-ball duo, combining for 10 missed tackles.

Personnel: Christian Benford, Davison Igbinosun, Dee Alford, Maxwell Hairston, Cole Bishop, C.J. Gardner-Johnson, Damar Hamlin

Demonstrated Strengths: Benford has generally recovered from an awful start to the season as the team's top cover man, while Igbinosun has made steady progress despite continuing to draw too many flags in his rookie campaign. Gardner-Johnson and Bishop have had a few nice moments, but that's about where the praise ends.

Needs Improvement: I mean, it's the NFL's 32nd-ranked pass defense. Benford has still given up his share of critical completions, and Hairston has already been benched in favor of mistake-prone rookie Igbinosun. Alford has struggled when healthy in his debut season with the Bills, while Bishop has severely lacked consistency in what was supposed to be a breakout campaign.

Meanwhile, only the Broncos (54) have more missed tackles than the Bills (44), with the vast majority of Buffalo's misses coming from the secondary.

Gardner-Johnson's tackling has been a particular concern, compounded by his ejection against the Raiders for spitting toward opposing players and the resulting one-game NFL suspension.

articles.title: Week 7 Waiver Wire Top Pickups and Drops Likely Available After Reviewing Box Scores
articles.summary: In most fantasy football leagues, winning requires smart in-season roster management and a bit of luck with the waiver wire. That's been especially true in 2026, as injuries have become a significant and consistent part of the fantasy conversation.
articles.body:
In most fantasy football leagues, winning requires smart in-season roster management and a bit of luck with the waiver wire. That's been especially true in 2026, as injuries have become a significant and consistent part of the fantasy conversation.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts recently joined the list of players who will be out for the remainder of the season, as he'll focus on treatment for blood clots. Davante Adams, Ladd McConkey, and Romeo Doubs were among the players who suffered injuries in Week 6.

Bye weeks have also entered the picture, and the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders will be off this week. Naturally, many managers will be looking to adjust rosters and pluck prime sleepers off the wire.

Here, we'll review recent performances and identify some top targets and drop candidates for point-per-reception (PPR) leagues.

Kyle Monangai (toe) didn't practice at all before he was ruled out for Week 6. That doesn't bode well for a potential Week 7 return. As long as Monangai remains sidelined, Chicago Bears backup Roschon Johnson should have some low-end flex value.

Chicago was able to run the ball frequently against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. This allowed Johnson to see a sizeable workload while spelling starter D'Andre Swift. He finished with 13 carries for 51 yards, two receptions, 34 receiving yards, and a touchdown.

Johnson's ceiling will be somewhat limited this week against the New England Patriots, who have allowed an average of just 17.9 fantasy points to opposing backfields. Still, Johnson should have a reasonable volume-based floor.

Johnson is rostered in only eight percent of fantasy leagues.

Add: Kendre Miller, RB, New Orleans Saints

New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller is in a situation similar to Johnson's. With Travis Etienne Jr. on injured reserve, Miller has a stable role in the Saints' backfield alongside Alvin Kamara.

Miller led the Saints with 70 yards on 20 carries in Week 6. He also had a pair of receptions.

While Miller's PPR floor is generally limited by Kamara's receiving role, Kamara aggravated a back injury in Week 6. If he's limited in Week 7, Miller is likely to see the bulk of the backfield work.

Like the Patriots, the Pittsburgh Steelers aren't the friendliest fantasy matchup—especially if the game is played in Paris as planned. However, Miller could see a starter's workload and is only rostered in 24 percent of fantasy leagues.

Tre Tucker remains rostered in only 47 percent of fantasy leagues, despite the fact that he has established himself as the Las Vegas Raiders' top perimeter target. While this hasn't always meant big fantasy production, Tucker came into Week 6 with four straight games of at least 7.5 fantasy points.

Tucker then proceeded to go off against the Buffalo Bills. He finished with five catches for 97 yards, two touchdowns, and 26.7 fantasy points.

Managers cannot expect Tucker to top 20 points every single week, but he has a lot of upside against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 7.

While the Rams have stumbled to a 2-4 record, they still have a potent offense that could force Las Vegas to play catch-up on the scoreboard—not unlike the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Los Angeles' defense could also be exploitable as Jaylen Watson battled a shoulder injury and Trent McDuffie works through a groin injury.

Add: Germie Bernard, WR, Pittsburgh Steelers

We highlighted Steelers receiver Germie Bernard as a high-upside sleeper last week . However, the rookie was even more productive than anticipated.

Bernard played a big role in Pittsburgh's comeback victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and he's quickly earned the trust of quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Against Tampa, he caught 11 of 12 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown.

While Bernard may not replicate his Week 6 numbers against New Orleans, he should again see a significant role. Michael Pittman Jr. is on injured reserve, while Roman Wilson is expected to miss multiple weeks.

For the time being, Bernard is Pittsburgh's No. 2 receiver opposite DK Metcalf. He'll be a very popular add this week, but he's only rostered in 36 percent of leagues right now.

articles.title: B/R's Week 7 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: They say time flies when you're having fun. And sure enough, once the dust settles on Week 7, the fantasy football regular season will be halfway over.
articles.body:
They say time flies when you're having fun. And sure enough, once the dust settles on Week 7, the fantasy football regular season will be halfway over.

Whether it has been fun or not is a matter of perspective.

Fantasy managers who drafted well and have avoided injuries are rolling along and piling up wins. For others, it has been a root canal minus the Novocain. The players who have managed to stay healthy have failed to meet expectations. The losses are stacked like firewood.

But whether you're 5-1 and partying like it's 1999 or 1-5 and drowning your sorrows, the goal this week is the same: log a victory.

We're all about making sure the trains run on time here at Bleacher Report, so we have everything you need for a Week 7 victory with position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start-or-sit recommendations and sleepers.

Before we get things rolling for Week 7 with a handy set of sortable PPR player rankings, a few notes.

The first is the same as always. The top 123 (it's my lucky number) players overall (a list that can aid in making "flex" lineup decisions) do not contain quarterbacks. If you play in a "superflex" format where quarterbacks are flex-eligible and you have a decent second signal-caller on the roster, he belongs in a flex spot.

The second is that the bye weeks roll on this week—the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers and Washington Commanders are all off. Sorry, no Joshua Patrick Allen in Week 7.

Finally, it can be incredibly frustrating to enter a season filled with hope only to start the year 2-4 or 1-5. But don't just throw up your hands, throw in the towel and start putting up Christmas decorations. It only takes a couple of wins to turn 2-4 into .500, and there's a lot of season left.

Make some waiver adds, set your strongest lineup and channel your inner LL Cool J to knock out the competition.

Over the summer, New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was the fourth player at his position drafted on average in fantasy leagues.

After a dreadful start to the season, Maye sat at QB34 in fantasy points —and the folks who invested in him were freaking out.

Fast-forward three more weeks, and those fantasy managers are breathing a lot easier. After throwing for 235 yards and three touchdowns in last week's win over the New York Jets, Maye has posted at least 23 fantasy points and scored at least three times in three straight weeks.

Over that span, Maye is the highest-scoring fantasy quarterback by a wide margin, and the third-year signal-caller is up to eighth at his position in points for the season.

The quarterback injury situation worsened in Week 6.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs after returning from the team's London game against Jacksonville, in which he played every offensive snap. He is taking blood thinners and is expected to miss the remainder of the season.

There could be some good news on the injury front in Week 7. After missing the last two games with an ankle injury, there is optimism that Lamar Jackson of the Baltimore Ravens will return to practice this week ahead of a pivotal AFC North matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals.

The Dallas Cowboys have lost three of four, in part because Dak Prescott and the offense are in a funk. After throwing four touchdown passes in Week 2, the quarterback has thrown just one scoring strike in four straight games. He's still inside the top-12 at the position in fantasy points, but just barely.

Jordan Love, Green Bay Packers (at Detroit Lions)

Over Green Bay's three-game winning streak, Love ranks sixth among quarterbacks in fantasy points. The good times should keep rolling Sunday against a Detroit defense that ranks last in the NFL in both total yards and passing yards allowed this season.

Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs (at Seattle Seahawks)

The Chiefs are undefeated this season, but Mahomes has been in a bit of a statistical funk of late—he hasn't posted more than 17 fantasy points in a game since Week 2. Now he draws a Seattle pass defense surrendering just 141.3 passing yards per contest in 2026.

Tanner McKee, Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Dallas Cowboys)

McKee was actually OK in his first start for the Eagles last week—he threw for 215 yards and a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers. He is a sneaky spot-starter in Week 7 against a Dallas defense giving up the fifth-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

At the rate he's going, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III is going to win a lot of fantasy managers leagues this season.

After roasting the Los Angeles Chargers for 128 yards and two scores on 19 carries last week, Walker leads the NFL in rushing—despite playing one fewer game than most backs. He is averaging a gaudy 6.3 yards per carry and 133 rushing yards per game, and he has found paydirt half-a-dozen times on the ground.

Walker has at least 115 rushing yards in four of five games. He has scored multiple touchdowns three times in five contests. And his 665 rushing yards over his first five games with the Chiefs is the most ever by a running back over his first five games with a team.

The good news is that there weren't any significant new injuries to running backs in Week 6. The bad news is that there are still a robust number of banged-up backs headlined by Saquon Barkley of the Philadelphia Eagles.

Barkley hasn't practiced since hurting his hamstring, and he's iffy at best for this week's visit from the rival Cowboys.

Jahmyr Gibbs of the Detroit Lions was unable to rampage once again in Week 6, but that's only because he was on a bye. He has been off the chain for fantasy managers this season—he's averaging 5.7 yards per touch, has a league-high nine total touchdowns and is the only player in all of fantasy averaging over 30 PPR points per game.

At the opposite end of the spectrum, Omarion Hampton of the Los Angeles Chargers has struggled to make a fantasy impact this season. After seven carries for 18 yards last week against the Chiefs, he has hit 15 PPR points just once in six games.

Dameon Pierce, Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Dallas Cowboys)

In the span of a few weeks, Pierce has gone from the practice squad to starting in the backfield for the injury-ravaged Eagles. Pierce is barely averaging over two yards per carry, but the Cowboys have the NFL's worst defense—Dallas is giving up just under 150 yards per game on the ground.

Chuba Hubbard, Carolina Panthers (vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

Hubbard has been excellent for fantasy managers this season—he's seventh among running backs in PPR points per game after six weeks. But the sledding won't be easy this week against the Buccaneers—Tampa has the NFC's stingiest run defense, allowing just 75.5 yards per game.

Bam Knight, Arizona Cardinals (vs. Denver Broncos)

Despite being short-handed in the backfield last week, the Cardinals stuck with a committee attack—Knight turned 17 touches into 98 total yards against the Los Angeles Rams. The Broncos have been generous to opposing running backs in 2026, giving up the sixth-most PPR points per game to the position.

In many respects, the top performers at wide receiver this year have been the usual suspects. Seeing Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seattle Seahawks, CeeDee Lamb of the Dallas Cowboys and Amon-Ra St. Brown of the Detroit Lions inside the top five after six weeks is no surprise.

However, seeing not one but two wide receivers from the Green Bay Packers inside the top 10 is another story.

Of late, it has been second-year pro Matthew Golden who has been on a rip. His six-catch, 104-yard, one-touchdown performance against Dallas last week marked his third 20-point outing in four weeks.

Christian Watson has done his part as well. He's third in PPR points at the position thanks to two outings with over 30 PPR points and 19.8 points per game.

No position has been hit harder by injuries this year than wide receiver, and those hits kept coming in Week 6. Terry McLaurin of the Washington Commanders suffered a season-ending patellar tendon tear Monday night, while Davante Adams of the Los Angeles Rams ruptured his hamstring and will be out indefinitely.

Mike Evans of the San Francisco 49ers left Monday's win over Washington with Achilles soreness. Romeo Doubs of the New England Patriots landed on injured reserve after injuring his shoulder. And Ladd McConkey's nightmare season continues—add a concussion to his long list of ailments.

It was a bad week for injuries, but it was a good one for rookie pass-catchers—both Germie Bernard of the Pittsburgh Steelers (11/87/1) and Omar Cooper Jr. of the New York Jets (6/103/1) landed among the top-10 wideouts in PPR points in Week 6.

DeVonta Smith, Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Dallas Cowboys)

Smith was the primary target and then some for Tanner McKee last week against the Panthers, turning a whopping 14 targets into seven catches for 75 yards and a touchdown. He's in the WR1 conversation again this week against the Dallas Cowboys and their struggling pass defense.

Omar Cooper Jr., New York Jets (vs. Miami Dolphins)

One of the Jets' three first-round picks last April, Cooper was as advertised last week against the Patriots. But Garrett Wilson is still the alpha wide receiver for Gang Green, and the Dolphins have surprisingly surrendered the third-fewest PPR points per game to wide receivers in 2026.

Brandin Cooks, San Francisco 49ers (at Atlanta Falcons)

With San Francisco dealing with multiple injuries at wide receiver, Cooks could play a significant role for the 49ers on Sunday against an Atlanta Falcons defense allowing the sixth-most PPR points per game to the position this season.

Over the summer, there was some disagreement over who the top tight end in fantasy football would be. But there were two candidates for the honor in 2026—Trey McBride of the Arizona Cardinals and Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders.

In terms of PPR points per game, Bowers is indeed No. 1 at the position. But in terms of total points, there's an un-Likely top dog.

Thanks to six catches for 99 yards and a touchdown last week against the New Orleans Saints, Isaiah Likely of the New York Giants is one of two tight ends who has already logged 100 fantasy points.

Fantasy managers who heeded the advice of fantasy pundits who pegged Likely as a breakout candidate in 2026 are reaping the rewards.

When Bowers returned to the Raiders' lineup in Week 3, most fantasy managers believed that Michael Mayer would retreat back into obscurity. But Mayer has actually been more productive with Bowers on the field—he's eighth among all tight ends in points over the last month.

Kyle Pitts of the Atlanta Falcons offered little fantasy production over the first month of the season, but he has heated up in recent weeks. His two-week total of 10 catches for 102 yards and three touchdowns puts him second in PPR points among tight ends over that span.

Fantasy managers got a scare in Week 6 when Dalton Kincaid of the Buffalo Bills left Sunday's wild win over the Raiders with a rib injury. However, fantasy's No. 11 tight end in PPR points through six weeks returned to the game, and with the Bills off in Week 7 he should be fine moving forward.

Tucker Kraft, Green Bay Packers (at Detroit Lions)

Green Bay's wide receivers are kicking tail and taking names, but Kraft has been rather disappointing in 2026. He's outside the top 12 at the position in PPR points after six weeks. But the Lions present a golden opportunity for a "get right" game—Detroit leads the league in PPR points per game allowed to tight ends by a wide margin.

Kyle Pitts, Atlanta Falcons (vs. San Francisco 49ers)

Pitts has produced well over the past couple of weeks, but a difficult matchup could limit his production this week. The Falcons face the San Francisco 49ers, who have allowed the fourth-fewest PPR points to tight ends this season.

A.J. Barner, Seattle Seahawks (vs. Kansas City Chiefs)

It has been a quiet year for Barner. He has amassed over eight PPR points in just one of six games this season. But this week gives him a chance for his second big outing of the year—the Chiefs have been kind to opposing tight ends this year, giving up the most fantasy points per game in the AFC to tight ends.

This analyst has long been a proponent of "streaming" team defenses based on matchups—so much changes from year-to-year (or even week-to-week) that last season's treasure can quickly become this year's trash.

Fantasy managers who invested in one of the top-three defenses in terms of ADP are finding that out the hard way in 2026.

Admittedly, the Denver Broncos have rebounded from a rough start. With three big outings over their last four contests, they have climbed all the way to third in points among defenses.

The Los Angeles Rams and Houston Texans, not so much. Whether due to injuries or just poor performance, they are both sitting outside the top 20 after six weeks.

Despite having already had their bye week, the Minnesota Vikings still lead all defenses in fantasy points and in fantasy points per game by a sizable margin. However, after this week's home date with the Indianapolis Colts the schedule tightens up—the Lions, Bills and Packers are Minnesota's next three opponents.

The Cincinnati Bengals spent big on the defensive side of the ball in the offseason, and that investment is paying off for fantasy managers six weeks into the season. The Bengals were also on a bye last week, but that hasn't stopped them from ranking a respectable seventh in fantasy points.

Six weeks into the season, there are two kickers averaging over 10 fantasy points per game, yet neither was drafted over the summer. Spencer Shrader of the Indianapolis Colts and Will Reichard of the Minnesota Vikings have combined for 33 field goal attempts—and made them all.

San Francisco 49ers Defense (at Atlanta Falcons)

The 49ers rank sixth among defenses in fantasy points after six weeks. The Falcons have given up the third-most fantasy points per game to defenses. You can't argue with math.

Ryan Fitzgerald, Carolina Panthers (vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

Fitzgerald has been OK for fantasy managers—he's ninth in fantasy points per game among kickers so far this season. Meanwhile, the Buccaneers are one of three teams giving up double-digit points per game to the position.

Seattle Seahawks Defense (vs. Kansas City Chiefs)

Just as they were in a march to a championship last year, the Seahawks are excellent on defense this year. But no team in the AFC has given up fewer fantasy points per game to defenses than the Chiefs this year.

Trey Smack, Green Bay Packers (at Detroit Lions)

Smack has had a couple of good games this year, but the Lions are so bad defensively that opponents aren't kicking field goals. Just two teams have allowed fewer fantasy points per game to kickers.

Carolina Panthers Defense (vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

The Panthers aren't especially good defensively, and most of their fantasy production came in a Week 2 blowout of the Atlanta Falcons. But Tampa leads the league in fantasy points per game allowed to team defenses in 2026.

Andre Szmyt, Cleveland Browns (at Tennessee Titans)

Szmyt hit the game-winner last week against the Baltimore Ravens. He has missed just once in two dozen-plus attempts. And the Titans have surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points per game to kickers this year.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: \Latest NFL Odds and Picks Factoring in New Weather Forecasts for Week 7 Schedule
articles.summary: We have one more full slate of October games on the schedule. While that's usually too early for NFL teams to be dealing with must-win scenarios, we are looking at a few of those in Week 7.
articles.body:
We have one more full slate of October games on the schedule. While that's usually too early for NFL teams to be dealing with must-win scenarios, we are looking at a few of those in Week 7.

The Los Angeles Rams, for example, fell to 2-4 on Sunday and can't afford another loss if they hope to remain relevant in the NFC West race. The Indianapolis Colts, meanwhile, just fired GM Chris Ballard and could make more significant changes if Indy slips to 2-5 this week.

The mounting pressure will be a factor for several teams. Weather is likely to impact a few more.

Here, we'll take an early look at the Week 7 slate, the latest odds, and the most accurate forecast information from The Weather Channel to make a few predictions.

New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears

Forecast: Mostly Clear Skies, Low of 51°F

Pittsburgh Steelers (-3) vs. New Orleans Saints (in Paris)

Forecast: Chance of Rain, Winds up to 20MPH, High of 60°F

San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons (Retractable Roof)

Cincinnati Bengals (+2.5) at Baltimore Ravens

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers

New York Giants (+9.5) at Houston Texans (Retractable Roof)

Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings (Dome)

Cleveland Browns (-1.5) at Tennessee Titans

Denver Broncos (-4.5) at Arizona Cardinals (Retractable Roof)

Green Bay Packers (+3) at Detroit Lions (Dome)

Los Angeles Rams (-4.5) at Las Vegas Raiders (Dome)

Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) at Seattle Seahawks

Dallas Cowboys (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles

Byes: Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders

If the early season is an accurate indication of what's to come, fans should probably expect the unexpected in Week 7.

Things will kick off with a Thursday night showdown between the Chicago Bears and New England Patriots. Caleb Williams returned to action for the Bears in Week 6, and Chicago's offense immediately returned to form. However, it's fair to wonder if the Bears' lackluster defense can corral the Patriots now that Drake Maye seems to have found his rhythm.

Sunday's action will begin at Sade de France in Paris, where the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers will face off. Pittsburgh is by far the better team on paper, but it needed to stage an epic comeback against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Playing overseas and against another mobile quarterback in Tyler Shough could give the Steelers trouble.

Right now, the Paris game looks like the only one that could be heavily impacted by weather. Of course, things can change rapidly in late October. Temperatures could be a factor in places like Arizona, Tennessee, and Houston, however.

Weather will be a total non-factor when the Green Bay Packers take on the rival Detroit Lions late Sunday afternoon. Detroit has a high-powered offense and will be coming out of its bye week. However, the Lions' defense has struggled, especially against the pass, and Green Bay's passing game has started to find its groove. This one is going to be fun.

Sunday's nightcap between the Kansas City Chiefs and Seattle Seahawks will also be intriguing. Seattle's defense and home-field advantage will be tough to overcome, but it's fair to wonder if Sam Darnold can break out of his funk against an aggressive Chiefs defense.

It would help if the Seahawks had a quality rushing attack, which they don't. Kansas City does, and it'll bring Kenneth Walker III back to Seattle for a "revenge" game.

Monday's battle between the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles lost some luster when the Eagles announced that quarterback Jalen Hurts would miss the rest of the season while getting treatment for blood clots. However, Saquon Barkley could return this week, which would give Philly a real shot against a struggling Cowboys defense.

articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 7
articles.summary: It may seem hard to believe, but we're barreling toward the midway point of the 2026 NFL season. Week 7 will kick off on Thursday, and the November 10 trade deadline isn't too far off.
articles.body:
It may seem hard to believe, but we're barreling toward the midway point of the 2026 NFL season. Week 7 will kick off on Thursday, and the November 10 trade deadline isn't too far off.

We're likely to see quite a bit of trade activity between now and the deadline, as several teams are becoming desperate for reinforcements. Several others are already on the verge of elimination.

The Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers remain winless. The struggling Indianapolis Colts, meanwhile, just fired general manager Chris Ballard.

It's not yet entirely clear which NFL teams will be the most aggressive buyers at the trade deadline. However, we have a much better idea of who those teams may target and which franchises are the most likely to sell.

Here, you'll find our updated list of top 10 trade candidates, ranked according to factors like past production, upside, positional value, contract/cap implications, projected availability, and any relevant recent rumors.

You'll also find projected trade values based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals, along with sensible potential suitors for each player.

10. Mason Rudolph, QB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 7th-Round Pick

Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar .

Jason La Canfora of Casino.org reported at the start of the season that Pittsburgh probably would have traded Rudolph then, had there been a viable market for him.

Of course, the Steelers are unlikely to find a strong market for Rudolph now, especially after the Atlanta Falcons added Andy Dalton for insurance. Quarterbacks like Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, and Baker Mayfield have already returned or are close to returning from injury.

Rudolph, who has made 20 career starts (including playoffs), will be most valuable if and when another team loses its starter for an extended period. That said, there are a few franchises that should view him as an upgrade over their current depth.

Potential Suitors: Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-Round Pick

The Philadelphia Eagles aren't entirely out of the playoff mix at 2-4, but they are expected to be without standout quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season.

The 28-year-old will undergo treatment for blood clots in his lungs, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

While Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has been an aggressive deadline buyer in the past, he could take the opposite approach because of this year's unique situation.

According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , some team executives are already wondering whether the Eagles could make Saquon Barkley and Riq Woolen available.

Philly might not want to part with Barkley, who should be the centerpiece of the offense once he's healthy. However, Woolen would be a very sensible trade chip.

The Eagles only signed Woolen to a one-year deal , and cornerbacks are typically in demand. Woolen, who has allowed a career opposing passer rating of just 73.8 , should draw a reasonable return, even for a short-term rental.

Potential Suitors: Buffalo Bills, Cincinnati Bengals

8. Daron Payne, DT, Washington Commanders

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick and/or a Veteran Receiver

The Washington Commanders are still scrapping for a spot in the NFC East race, as evidenced by their admirable comeback effort against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night.

"It's still wide open," receiver Stefon Diggs told Marshall Kramsky of WUSA.

However, effort doesn't change the fact that Washington is sitting at 1-4-1 and just lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin to a season-ending knee injury . Getting the season back on track will be a challenge.

If the Commanders are open to trading players, possibly for receiver help, Daron Payne is a strong candidate. The 29-year-old defensive tackle has started all six games this season, has recorded 14 tackles, and will interest teams seeking defensive-line help.

Payne is also in a contract year and carrying a cap hit of $28 million .

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, Jacksonville Jaguars

Projected Trade Value: 2027 5th-Round Pick

The Tennessee Titans got their first win of the season on Sunday with an upset of the rival Colts.

That victory should ease some of the pressure on head coach Robert Saleh and quarterback Cam Ward, but it doesn't mean Tennessee is on the verge of turning its season around.

The Titans are still very much a struggling squad. Ward threw for just 102 yards in Indy, and Tennessee would most likely still be winless if not for multiple mistakes by the Colts—including three turnovers and a massive special-teams blunder .

GM Mike Borgonzi should still be thinking long-term, and the plan should involve either replacing Ward or putting more pieces around him. Either way, flipping expiring contracts for draft capital would be logical.

Running back Tony Pollard is a good support piece for Ward right now, but he's 29 years old and an impending free agent. He should have a solid trade market, though, as he has four 1,000-yard seasons on his resume and could upgrade several of the backfields that have been impacted by injuries this season.

Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Seattle Seahawks

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick

The Arizona Cardinals just pulled off their second massive upset of the season, beating the Rams in Los Angeles 18-16.

The big divisional win should give Arizona some confidence in its ability to compete this season, but the Cardinals know they're largely playing for the future.

Otherwise, general manager Monti Ossenfort wouldn't have agreed to trade receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. Ossenfort will likely consider making other moves ahead of the deadline, and pass-rusher Josh Sweat is a prime trade candidate to track.

The Cardinals' GM dismissed the idea of moving Sweat during the offseason, but stronger offers could come in-season as teams gear up for a playoff run. Sweat, who has two sacks, three tackles for loss, and seven quarterback pressures this season, should draw significant interest.

While Sweat can help the Cardinals now, he also looms as a likely 2027 cap casualty. Arizona can release him with a post-June 1 designation in the spring and save $18.1 million in cap space next offseason.

Potential Suitors: Baltimore Ravens, Cleveland Browns

The Miami Dolphins have parted with several key veterans since last year's trade deadline. However, longtime defensive lineman Zach Sieler has made it clear that he hopes he isn't the next veteran to go.

"I know people say rumors or talk whatever this time of year, but I'm here focused playing games here, win as a Dolphin, man," Sieler said, per the team's official website .

Of course, Sieler's wishes may not matter much to new GM Jon-Eric Sullivan if and when offers for the versatile defender begin to come. Sieler is signed through 2029 but could be a realistic 2027 cap casualty for Miami.

$10 million of Sieler's salary will become fully guaranteed on the third day of the 2027 league year. Releasing him with a post-June 1 designation before then would save the Dolphins $13.2 million in cap space.

Teams are almost always on the lookout for defensive-line help. Sieler, who has 12 tackles, two sacks, and five tackles for loss this year, can provide it.

Potential Suitors: Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings

4. DeForest Buckner, DT, Indianapolis Colts

Projected Trade Value: 2027 4th-Round Pick

Ballard is already out, and at this point, it's hard to imagine that Colts head coach Shane Steichen survives beyond the regular season.

Interim general manager Ed Dodds—along with franchise ownership—may soon consider selling off pieces, as the Miami Dolphins did after firing GM Chris Grier last season.

DeForest Buckner would be a logical trade chip if that is the case. Premier defensive tackles generally command strong returns, and Buckner is still one of those, even at 32.

Buckner has started all six games for Indianapolis this season and has tallied 26 tackles, four sacks, three passes defended, and nine quarterback pressures. However, he's unhappy with Indy's ability to contend.

"I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Buckner told reporters after Sunday's loss to the Titans.

The three-time Pro Bowler is also playing in the final year of his current contract. Trading him would provide some cap relief while allowing the Colts to acquire something in return for a player who could leave in free agency next spring.

Potential Suitors: Green Bay Packers, San Francisco 49ers

3. Landon Dickerson, G, Philadelphia Eagles

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 2nd-Round Pick

The Eagles have already dealt center Cam Jurgens, and if they decide that they can't salvage the 2026 season, another talented offensive lineman could be on the move.

According to Schefter, some around the league believe standout guard Landon Dickerson could be available.

"It would not surprise those in the league if teams start calling on Eagles guard Landon Dickerson when he is healthy enough to return from injured reserve," Schefter wrote .

Dickerson remains sidelined with a bone bruise in his right knee. However, he's a three-time Pro Bowler and one of the league's better interior linemen when he's at 100 percent. He'd provide a big upgrade for multiple playoff hopefuls who are getting questionable play along the offensive interior.

Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Houston Texans

2. Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Projected Trade Value: 2027 2nd- and 6th-Round Picks

Unlike most deadline sellers, the Jacksonville Jaguars are very much in the playoff picture at 4-2. However, they're still in a position to move off of a promising young player.

2024 first-round pick Brian Thomas Jr. was a Pro Bowler as a rookie but has regressed in a big way since. He's largely fallen out of the game plan this year and was seemingly benched for the second half of Sunday's loss to the Texans.

While GM James Gladstone discounted the idea of trading Thomas during the offseason, his stance may have changed in the wake of the Harrison trade. After all, if Arizona can get a strong return for an underachieving receiver, Gladstone should at least consider doing the same.

According to ESPN's Dan Graziano, many around the league believe he will.

"There are a lot of people around the league who believe Thomas could have a new home by the trade deadline," Graziano wrote .

Teams that need receiver help will and should make a run at Thomas.

Potential Suitors: Seattle Seahawks, Washington Commanders

1. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

On Saturday, The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported that the Los Angeles Chargers are still trying to rebuff trade offers.

"Teams are calling Chargers GM Joe Hortiz, who has told multiple GMs the same thing about any potential trade offers: We're not interested," Pelissero wrote in his Substack, The Sweep .

However, Los Angeles fell to 0-6 on Sunday, and it would be irresponsible at this point for Hortiz to not at least consider offers that could help the franchise's long-term plans.

Pass-rusher Khalil Mack is the most logical trade chip the Chargers have because he's playing on a one-year deal and because he plays a premium position well.

The 35-year-old has started all six games for L.A. this season and has recorded 19 tackles, three sacks, five tackles for loss, and 11 quarterback pressures. Teams that need a disruptive edge-defender for the playoff run should have Mack at or near the top of their wish lists.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, San Francisco 49ers

articles.title: Week 7 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Review for Fantasy Football's Top Fringe Starters
articles.summary: Another week of NFL action is in the books, and another round of notable injuries is set to impact the fantasy football landscape.
articles.body:
Another week of NFL action is in the books, and another round of notable injuries is set to impact the fantasy football landscape.

Ladd McConkey, Davante Adams, Terry McLaurin, Romeo Doubs, and Rashod Bateman were among those who exited with injuries in Week 6. In Week 7, managers may have to navigate their injuries, others, and a host of fantasy stars on bye.

The Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders will have the week off.

Here, you'll find start/sit recommendations for some fringe starters who could be in line to help fill the void. All picks are based on recent results, projected roles, individual matchups, and point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

A few rough early-season games have kept Jordan Love away from must-start territory, and he's still only rostered in 80 percent of leagues. However, the Green Bay Packers quarterback has started to find a rhythm with receivers Matthew Golden and Christian Watson and is on an upward trajectory because of it.

Love has topped 21 fantasy points in each of the past two weeks. He should have another strong outing this week when the Packers visit the rival Detroit Lions.

Detroit is coming off its bye and will have home-field advantage, but no team has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing QBs.

It's probably time for managers to abandon Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold, at least for the time being. He was miserable against the Denver Broncos in Week 6 and has looked nothing like the Pro Bowl signal-caller he was a year ago.

Darnold has topped 20 fantasy points only once this season.

Things won't get any easier for Darnold this week against the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. The Chiefs have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing QBs.

With Breece Hall sidelined by a quad injury, Braelon Allen has done a fine job of replacing him as the New York Jets' starter. He has topped 12 fantasy points in back-to-back games, and he's likely to have another strong outing in Week 7.

That is, if Hall doesn't make an unexpected return.

The Jets are set to host the Miami Dolphins, who have surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season.

Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard has traditionally been a serviceable volume-based running back. However, he has struggled along with the rest of Tennessee's offense this season and has gone consecutive weeks without a reception.

While Pollard has topped 13 fantasy points twice this season, he has fallen short of eight points in each of the last two weeks.

This week, the Titans will host an aggressive Cleveland Browns defense that will likely force Cam Ward to beat it. The Browns have surrendered the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs.

Cleveland Browns rookie receiver Denzel Boston was a budding fantasy star but ran into a proverbial wall in Week 6. He had topped 12 fantasy points in four of his first five games but was limited to one 15-yard catch by the Baltimore Ravens.

However, Boston should rebound this week against the Tennessee Titans.

The Titans have a vastly underrated run defense, and the Browns have struggled to run the ball effectively, anyway. Cleveland should look to pass early and often against a defense that has yielded the 10th-most fantasy points to opposing receivers.

Devaughn Vele has emerged as the New Orleans Saints' second option at receiver and a viable flex streamer in fantasy. He had a modest three catches and 42 yards in Week 6, but he has reached double-digit fantasy points in three of his first six outings.

However, Vele should be considered a matchup-based play, and he does not have a favorable matchup in Week 7.

The Saints will play the Pittsburgh Steelers, who have surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing WRs this season.

Los Angeles Rams tight end Tyler Higbee lost a fumble in Sunday's loss to the Arizona Cardinals and finished with just 2.2 fantasy points. However, the Rams lost No. 2 receiver Davante Adams to a hamstring injury, which could effectively make Higbee the No. 2 target next to Puka Nacua.

That would be an advantageous role against a Las Vegas Raiders defense that has surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season.

Higbee, by the way, topped nine fantasy points in three straight games before Sunday's disaster.

Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts is coming off a monster game (5 catches, 60 yards, 2 TDs) against the Chicago Bears, and he has reached double-digit fantasy points in consecutive weeks. However, he simply hasn't consistently been a focal point of Atlanta's offense this season.

Pitts failed to reach eight fantasy points in each of the first four weeks.

While there is a chance that Kevin Stefanski has finally figured out how to utilize Pitts, betting on that in Week 7 is a gamble. The Falcons will host the San Francisco 49ers, who have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing TEs.

*Fantasy scoring information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Forget Jay-Z for the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show? These 3 artists could be better choices
articles.summary: Jay-Z has picked himself as the Super Bowl 2027 halftime show headliner. Puck’s Dave Brooks broke the news.
articles.body: Jay-Z has picked himself as the Super Bowl 2027 halftime show headliner. Puck’s Dave Brooks broke the news. His sources called the move “inevitable” and “more compelling” than Miley Cyrus or Justin Bieber, who were both under consideration. Jay-Z has a hand in picking the act, and he is touring stadiums this year. Still, not everyone is thrilled. Here are three artists who would make the 2027 halftime show feel fresher than a 56-year-old rapper replaying his hits.Why Miley Cyrus is a better choice than Jay-ZJay-Z has the momentum. His stadium run across North America marks 30 years of Reasonable Doubt and 25 years of The Blueprint, and the dates have sold out. But a halftime crowd is not a tour crowd. It is bigger and far less nostalgic.Cyrus was reportedly in the mix too, and she would be a first-time halftime performer with a catalog built for a stadium. Her new album, Bass Persuades, is out, and a crowd that wants to dance would rather hear “Flowers” and “Party in the U.S.A.” than a hip-hop throwback. The second song also happens to suit Los Angeles.She is also fresh off a comeback. Cyrus returned to the stage at the Hollywood Bowl earlier this month, four years after her last major concert.And she can slow things down. During her sold-out Los Angeles shows, she sang Dolly Parton’s “Jolene” as a tribute to her late godmother. “Me and Dolly, we are eternal. Nothing in this life could tear us apart,” Cyrus said through tears. A halftime show needs a moment like that between the big singalongs.Harry Styles suits the stage and the cityStyles is another mainstream pick, and that is partly the point. Hip-hop has had plenty of halftime time already, so a pop star with wide appeal is a fair swing. He has moved through several sounds since One Direction. His third album won a Grammy. His latest, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally, leans on electronica and is not his most convincing work.Still, the songs travel well. “As It Was,” “Watermelon Sugar” and “Adore You” are made for a crowd. Add “American Girls” and “Kiwi” and you have a set that moves. A February night in Los Angeles would have suited him.The bigger question is timing. Styles will get a call eventually. This year just happened to go to Jay-Z.Kelly Clarkson has the voice and the buzzClarkson is the best pure singer of the three. That voice turned “Since U Been Gone,” “Because of You,” “Breakaway” and “Miss Independent” into hits in the early 2000s, and “Stronger (What Doesn’t Kill You)” still gets a room shouting.She is also in the news right now, though not for music. Clarkson has been in a high-profile feud with Art of Play, a Brooklyn toy shop, and The New York Times covered it earlier this month. Her fans, known as Kellebrities, would not need convincing either.None of these three is getting the call this February. Jay-Z picked himself, and that settles it. articles.title: Jalen Hurts blood clot controversy takes another turn as NFL clears Eagles of wrongdoing despite growing scrutiny
articles.summary: The NFL has closed the book on how the Eagles handled Jalen Hurts’ blood clots.
articles.body: The NFL has closed the book on how the Eagles handled Jalen Hurts’ blood clots. League officials told The Athletic the team broke no rules by playing the quarterback against Jacksonville in London on Oct. 11, a day after doctors found a superficial clot in his calf. Days later, scans showed multiple clots in his lungs, and Hurts is now out indefinitely. The finding landed Tuesday, the same day the NFL Players Association demanded a full investigation. The league sees no problem. The union says nobody has actually checked.NFL clears Eagles over Jalen Hurts blood clot decisionThe league’s conclusion is short. It called the process “handled appropriately by the Eagles” and found no injury report violation. Jalen Hurts appeared on the report with a calf issue two days before kickoff but carried no game designation, since the team expected him to play without limits. He did. Hurts threw 21 of 40 for 220 yards and a touchdown in a 19-17 loss.The sleep story took the most heat, and it has now been walked back. Early reports said Hurts stayed awake 36 hours before the game. The Athletic says that is wrong. The whole team stayed on U.S. time during the trip, and his hospital visit stretched the night. A source told Yahoo Sports he returned to the hotel at 2:45 a.m., slept until 10, then napped again at the stadium instead of joining warmups.League doctors defend the medical processNFL chief medical officer Alan Sills went further. He argued that a bad outcome does not prove a bad process. Sometimes, he said, doctors do everything right and a disease still advances. In his words, everyone involved was “incredibly conservative and incredibly vigilant.” He added that most people would have gone longer without a diagnosis.There is medical support for part of that view. Two independent experts told Yahoo Sports it is rare for a superficial clot to move into a deep vein and then the lungs. Those clots usually stay put, and they do not normally rule a player out of contact sports. Once the clot spread, though, blood thinners became necessary, and that treatment runs three to six months.The Eagles say Jalen Hurts should recover fully, with no long-term effects.Union wants an outside lookThe NFLPA is not buying the league’s version. In a Tuesday night statement, it said it knew of no investigation into Hurts’ care and that the league had earlier told it none was planned. Conclusions, the union said, should wait for a full inquiry.That is the weak spot in the NFL’s position. Executive vice president Jeff Miller said the league spoke with Eagles staff, the independent hospital and the doctors involved, and has a complete picture. Talking to people is not the same as auditing records, and the union wants the records opened.Coach Nick Sirianni has made his own defense, pointing to the staff that kept 21 of 22 starters available for the Super Bowl. “Full trust in those guys,” he said. Some fans and reporters wanted general manager Howie Roseman or a team doctor to answer questions instead.For now, the Eagles have bigger problems on the field. articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Shane Steichen's Hot Seat as Colts HC After Chris Ballard's Firing as GM
articles.summary: Having already fired general manager Chris Ballard amid a 2-4 start to the season, Shane Steichen's future as head coach of the Indianapolis Colts is now being monitored around the NFL.
articles.body:
Having already fired general manager Chris Ballard amid a 2-4 start to the season, Shane Steichen's future as head coach of the Indianapolis Colts is now being monitored around the NFL.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano , Steichen's job is not believed to be in immediate danger after Ballard's dismissal.

According to Fowler, the "sentiment as of now" is the Colts will give Steichen a chance to "state his case" to remain head coach going forward.

Graziano added Steichen is "well-regarded" by people in the organization, but it is a "situation worth monitoring for potential change at the end of the season, if not sooner."

Ballard was fired one day after the Colts' 26-20 loss to the previously-winless Tennessee Titans on Sunday. The move marked the end of his 10-year tenure with the club that produced a 72-82-1 record and two playoff appearances.

Indianapolis' five-year playoff drought coming into this season was tied with the New Orleans Saints for the third-longest active drought in the NFL.

It was a little surprising the Colts opted not to do a full housecleaning by firing Steichen since there were already rumblings about his job status at the end of last season after they lost seven straight games following an 8-2 start.

Steichen is 27-30 as Colts head coach since being hired after the 2022 season. He had a winning record at 9-8 in his first year, but has finished under .500 in the past two seasons and is on pace to do so again in 2026.

There's certainly an argument that the recent failures for the Colts are more attributable to Ballard than Steichen.

Some of those moves include trading away two first-round picks for Sauce Gardner; giving Daniel Jones a two-year, $88 million contract in March, four months removed from tearing his Achilles; and signing Alec Pierce to a four-year, $116 million contract right before he underwent ankle surgery.

Pierce has only played in two games this season due to a heel injury related to his offseason surgery. Jones ranks 30th out of 33 qualified quarterbacks in QBR.

Steichen hasn't been helping the situation, at least in obvious ways. Their loss to the Titans included giving up 20 points in the fourth quarter, including a touchdown on a blocked punt.

Since the Colts are already in the market for a new general manager, it's not often that an incoming executive retains the head coach from the previous regime.

If the Colts are using the next few weeks as an evaluation period for Steichen, the schedule doesn't do him any favors. Their next two games are on the road against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings and AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: NFL Legend Calvin Johnson Talks Comeback, Stafford, Josh Allen, Lions and More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Calvin Johnson sees Matthew Stafford and Aaron Rodgers thriving in the latter stages of their careers. He also saw Aaron Donald and Philip Rivers recently come out of retirement.
articles.body:
Calvin Johnson sees Matthew Stafford and Aaron Rodgers thriving in the latter stages of their careers. He also saw Aaron Donald and Philip Rivers recently come out of retirement.

"No, I'm done," the 41-year-old told Bleacher Report while laughing. "I'm 10 years out. But it's fun to keep watching Matthew and even to see Philip Rivers come back. I played against Philip in my college days. Aaron Donald looks like he's still going to have an impact for that team. It's awesome to see them all still perform at a high level."

Johnson is partially remembered for a stunning retirement that came after his age-30 season, which was his sixth straight with more than 1,000 receiving yards. Detroit Lions fans have surely dreamed of a comeback ever since he walked away so early, but that is not going to happen.

Instead, they will have to reminisce over some of the most memorable highlights in NFL history.

Johnson was unguardable with the combination of size at 6'5" to make contested catches and speed to get past press coverage at the line of scrimmage. He is still the Lions' all-time leader in catches (731), receiving yards (11,619) and touchdown catches (83) and holds the NFL record for the most receiving yards in a single season with 1,964 in 2012.

The end result of his legendary career was an induction into the Hall of Fame as part of the 2021 class.

His former teammate in Stafford will eventually join him in Canton, Ohio, especially after he won a Super Bowl with the Los Angeles Rams during the 2021 campaign and then took home the MVP in 2025 in his age-37 season.

"I was happy for him," Johnson said. "The work he's put in over time, the work he put in with Detroit, to the Super Bowl he won in LA. The level of experience he has carries him a long way. For him to be able to go out there and continue to do it year after year is great."

While Stafford has added to his legacy with the Rams, he will always be linked together with Johnson after they played together for the Lions for seven years. Johnson led the league in receiving yards twice during that span, and the combination led the 2011 Detroit team to the playoffs to snap a franchise streak of 11 straight years without a postseason appearance.

The current-day Lions are in a much different spot, though, under head coach Dan Campbell.

They finished with a winning record in each of the previous four seasons, including when they reached the NFC Championship Game in the 2023 campaign and then went 15-2 in the 2024 season.

It is a notable run of success for a franchise that has never made the Super Bowl and was long known as a struggling club, but much of the same offensive core with Jared Goff, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, among others, have been in place for the last few years and will be expected to eventually take the next step.

"They're probably feeling some of the pressure," Johnson said of his former team. "People put pressure on you from the outside, but within the organization I'm sure everything is smooth and flowing in the right direction with the way they performed the last couple of weeks.

"The offense is coming around. Drew Petzing is doing better and better, it seems like he's getting comfortable with his guys and getting to know them pretty well. Defense is my sticking point, just making sure that secondary doesn't get exposed. I know Brian Branch is supposed to be coming back, which is great. But we know that can be an issue for us, so just make sure we cover that."

Detroit is off to a solid 3-2 start behind an offense that has thrived under a new offensive coordinator in Petzing and is tied with the Buffalo Bills for the most points per game at 32.8.

If a defense that is 30th in the league in points allowed per game plays at even an average level moving forward, it isn't unrealistic to expect the Lions to contend for their first Super Bowl in franchise history with Johnson cheering them on in retirement.

They aren't the only high-powered offense the Hall of Famer is paying attention to this season, as he also enjoys watching Josh Allen and the Bills.

"I am a Josh Allen fan," he said. "I would like to see him—as long as it's not against my Lions—get himself one. I think he's been a great player for a long time in this league. He's well-deserving of one. So hopefully they can get him over the edge as long as it's not against the Lions."

Like Detroit, Buffalo has never won a Super Bowl despite coming close in recent years. In fact, the Bills have reached the playoffs seven times and the AFC Championship Game twice since Allen took over as the full-time starter during the 2018 season.

The only thing truly missing from his resume that includes a league MVP and four Pro Bowl selections is a Super Bowl ring, which would further cement him as a future Hall of Famer and franchise icon.

While Johnson is watching the Lions and Bills in retirement and no longer playing, he is still focused on keeping his energy up and taking care of his health.

With that in mind, he partnered with Hims to help the company's efforts to drop the stigma around aging, energy and testosterone.

"We're all going to age, and with that there are going to be changes in our body," Johnson said. "My biggest thing is just keeping my energy levels up. I've got three boys at home, and being able to do the things they want to do and get outside and not feel sluggish is key."

Hims is revealing its largest testosterone expansion yet with injectable testosterone replacement therapy in compounded and commercial formulations, which builds on what it was already offering.

"Hims is being proactive," Johnson said. "A lot of men, we get kind of lax in terms of taking care of our health. Especially with me being a former professional athlete, I can speak to it. You almost feel untouchable while you're playing. But soon after you're done playing, all the aches and pains start to add up. Even more than that, energy levels start to decline sometimes. Being able to know where you're at and understand there is help out there can get you back to peak performance."

Few wide receivers in NFL history know what peak performance on the field looks like better than Johnson, and he continues to watch St. Brown carry on his legacy as an unstoppable Lions wide receiver.

He also loves watching Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson play as two of the best in the game, although Carolina Panthers star Tetairoa McMillan has also caught his attention.

"I like some of the young talent too," Johnson said. "Tet McMillan, he's a player. He reminds me of myself as a big guy who can run. But he uses his hands. That's what strikes my interest, a guy who uses his hands out there. I look forward to watching the rest of his career. He's young and in that second year, so he should have a big year this year and keep figuring it out. The second year for receivers is usually big."

McMillan is a 6'4" playmaker who can beat defenses with his speed or his physicality as a threat in the red zone. He is a star receiver who has immediately elevated the ceiling for a team that has struggled in the past, which is something Johnson can certainly relate to following his time in Detroit.

The No. 8 overall pick of the 2025 NFL draft already won the Offensive Rookie of the Year in his first year and turned heads against the Lions this season with 14 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns.

He also earned the respect of one of the franchise's all-time greats in the process.

articles.title: 'This is F--ked Up,' Travis Kelce Tells Funny Story About Taylor Swift Being Woken Up By Jason Kelce
articles.summary: Jason Kelce's dedication to early-morning workouts resulted in an amusing moment in the Travis Kelce-Taylor Swift household.
articles.body:
Jason Kelce's dedication to early-morning workouts resulted in an amusing moment in the Travis Kelce-Taylor Swift household.

On the latest episode of the New Heights podcast (starts 2:25 mark), Travis revealed he got a call from Jason at 7:30 a.m. one morning asking him for a spot.

"I'm, like, walking out of the room and Taylor's like, 'this is f--ked up,'" Travis said.

Jason has been participating in "Squatober", a themed-exercise program that takes place throughout the month of October. It encourages people to do squat-based activities five days per week throughout the entire month.

In addition to the squatting workouts, Jason is also doing other traditional exercises. This particular instance of waking up Swift, according to Travis, stemmed from his brother needing a spotter on the bench press.

Jason was staying at Travis and Taylor's house in the Kansas City area after taking part in a New Heights tailgate that was held around Arrowhead Stadium prior to Sunday's game between the Chiefs and Los Angeles Chargers.

The event didn't start until 11 a.m. local time, despite a 3:25 p.m. CT kickoff, but fans were reportedly lined up hours ahead of time to get the chance to partake in the festivities that included Jason signing autographs and shooting baskets.

articles.title: Joey Bosa predicted to make NFL comeback with brother Nick Bosa’s San Francisco 49ers as retirement rumors intensify
articles.summary: Joey Bosa retirement rumors have been circulating throughout the 2026 offseason. They may have halted for a second into the season.
articles.body: Joey Bosa retirement rumors have been circulating throughout the 2026 offseason. They may have halted for a second into the season.But with six games and no Nick Bosa in the San Francisco 49ers for four of those - the rumors are back in action. Only this time, there’s a spice of an NFL comeback. With midseason urgency.Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay has identified Joey Bosa as a potential addition for San Francisco. The 49ers are navigating defensive-line injury concerns; the veteran edge rusher could become an ideal solution for a team looking to strengthen its pass rush during the 2026 NFL season.Joey Bosa’s reunion with Nick Bosa in San Francisco 49ersThe San Francisco 49ers need to generate more consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks. The team has recorded 15 sacks in six games - this is a league-average mark that screams improvement.Nick Bosa’s Week 2 calf injury has severely affected the franchise’s ability to attack quarterbacks from the edge. Signing Nick Bosa’s older brother, Joey Bosa, could help address that weakness. Not just that, but also pursue a forever dream of championship success.The 49ers’ possibility of signing Joey carries more than just professional significance. It also carries a personal touch: the brothers haven’t played together since their high school days. That was in 2012. Their mother, Cheryl Bosa, really hopes to see Joey in a San Francisco 49ers jersey, just like her other son, Nick.Joey is a former Los Angeles Chargers edge defender who represented the Buffalo Bills in 2025. He recorded 5.0 sacks, 5 forced fumbles, 16 quarterback hits, and 9 tackles for loss in 15 games during the 2025 season.He had signed a one-year, $12M contract with the Bills in March 2025.
