articles.title: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Suspended by NFL for Spitting at Raiders, Joins CJGJ in Missing Week 8
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. landed in some hot water for an incident during the team's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. landed in some hot water for an incident during the team's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

The NFL announced that Franklin has been suspended for one game for "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" after he was seen spitting at an opponent in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game. The Bills are on a bye this week, so Franklin will miss their Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Franklin "is denying the allegation and will appeal."

NFL player suspended for spitting on opponent

Franklin joined the Bills' practice squad prior to the 2025 season and quickly earned a spot on the main roster. He appeared in all 17 games last season, mostly on special teams. He was voted a team captain this season.

While Franklin is denying the allegation, it seems like the Bills had a hard time keeping their mouths shut during Sunday's contest. Veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson also received a one-game suspension after cameras caught him spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum.

"C.J. knows that it's hard enough to win in this league with 48 guys, much less 47. He knows that that can't happen. It's inexcusable. That's not the standard that we're going to have and play with," Bills head coach Joe Brady told reporters on Monday. "He's addressed it. It's been addressed. The league came down with the suspension. … We want to toe the line with everything we do but we can't cross the line."

Gardner-Johnson addressed the incident with his teammates and coaches after the game, and he posted an apology for his actions on social media.

"My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he wrote. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game."

The Bills will try to focus on avoiding any further incidents during their bye week before returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

articles.title: Buccaneers rumors: Baker Mayfield injury return will be determined by 1 thing at practice
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could really use a shot in the arm. Tampa only has one win on the season after missing Baker Mayfield in their last few games. The l...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could really use a shot in the arm. Tampa only has one win on the season after missing Baker Mayfield in their last few games. The latest injury update on Tampa's franchise quarterback makes it perfectly clear what he needs to do before returning to the field.

NFL insider Ian Rapoport gave another injury update on Mayfield leading up to Week 7. The veteran quarterback's availability this week all depends on one displaying one simple skill in practice.

"Baker Mayfield, the Bucs quarterback, is expected to be on the practice field. He has missed three weeks, he's dealing with a dislocated thumb," Rapoport said on Tuesday via NFL Live. "It is a very simple thing: can he grip the ball and throw it? If he can, he is expected to play. If he cannot, it'll be another week of Jalon Daniels in Tampa."

Mayfield has already missed three games this season with this thumb injury. Fortunately, the rookie Daniels has played well in relief of Mayfield. In fact, Tampa's only win on the season came at the hands of their undrafted rookie.

Earlier this week, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles seemed to hint that Daniels could remain the starter in Week 7.

"(Todd) Bowles said Wednesday will be important for evaluating Baker Mayfield and his thumb but they'll plan as if Jalon Daniels is starting again in terms of initial game-planning," Greg Auman of FOX Sports reported on Monday.

Tampa may only be 1-5 on the season, but they are still only a few games back in the NFC South standings. That means they could feel pressure to get Mayfield back quickly to help save their season. Especially with a crucial divisional showdown coming up this weekend.

articles.title: ‘Don’t do this’ – Shannon Sharpe hammers the NFL after what they’ve said about Jalen Hurts
articles.summary: The Jalen Hurts health scare story has gripped the NFL with serious concerns being raised about the players’ welfare being shown by teams. The Philadelphia E...
articles.body:
The Jalen Hurts health scare story has gripped the NFL with serious concerns being raised about the players' welfare being shown by teams.

The Philadelphia Eagles' quarterback will not play again this season after it was discovered that he had blood clots in his lungs. How the diagnosis came about is what has really frustrated people around the league.

Hurts was allowed to fly to and from London despite there being an undiagnosed issue. That issue turned out to be blood clots which has now seen the quarterback forced to miss the remainder of the season.

Given the severity of the health scare, the NFL addressed the protocols taken by the Eagles' staff in a recent meeting with the media. However, Shannon Sharpe has been left furious with some of their answers.

Shannon Sharpe criticises NFL over Jalen Hurts assessment

The NFL has come to the conclusion that the Eagles did not violate the injury report policy and will, therefore, not be fined for allowing Hurts to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

"I love the NFL… but I hate when they do this. Don't do this," Sharpe said on the Nightcap show.

"If I'm not mistaken, the way I read it is that you wait till you get to London to do the MRI, and then you're like, 'Oh, okay.' Tell me the professional says that you should be flying even with a superficial blood clot. Wouldn't you think you would let him clear that up? Because knowing that it could travel to your lungs, it could travel to your heart.

Questions are going to be asked as the weeks go on as to why Hurts was allowed to travel and play in the London game despite the NFL's conclusion as Nick Sirianni passed on a number of opportunities to comment on the situation earlier in the week.

It is clear to see that former NFL stars like Sharpe have not been impressed with what they have seen unfold over the last few days.

articles.title: Week 7 NFL Power Rankings: Does close scare drop 49ers this week?
articles.summary: Are the Niners still deserving of the top spot in the power rankings?
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have been sitting atop the NFL's power rankings for a few weeks now, as they remain just one of three unbeaten teams in the league.

That remained true after Week 6, as the 49ers escaped by the Washington Commanders 23-17 in a game that went down to the final plays as the defense made a stand. San Francisco really struggled to generate offense without Mike Evans, while Jayden Daniels threw for 300 yards against the 49ers defense, leading to a closer game.

Nonetheless, San Francisco is 6-0, becoming the lone team in the NFL to win six games thus far. Given how close the game was and how other teams fared this weekend, did the 49ers get docked in the power rankings this week?

Let's look at several Week 7 power rankings to see the consensus.

The 49ers remained the top team here as they remain one of the teams without many actual flaws with their play. When highlighting the team's biggest issue on offense so far, the answer was clear: receiver injuries.

"The Niners haven't had many problems in terms of production, but they have had a significant amount of attrition at wideout," ESPN's Nick Wagoner wrote. Ricky Pearsall (knee), De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle), Christian Kirk (calf) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) were supposed to be four of the team's top five receivers and all landed on IR before Week 3.

"That doesn't account for Deebo Samuel Sr.'s multiweek hamstring injury or the various bumps and bruises Mike Evans played through before departing Monday night's game with Achilles tendinitis. The good news? Most of them are expected back this season, but the 49ers have had to scramble in the meantime."

Behind the 49ers were the Kansas City Chiefs, who improved to 5-0 off a dominant win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Rounding out the top five were the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings, and the Jacksonville Jaguars.

NFL.com's Nick Shook did note that there could be some question to San Francisco's standing atop the rankings after the win, but kept them at No. 1 still after six weeks over the Chiefs.

"San Francisco flirted with an epic collapse, but the same battered defensive line came through again in the final moments, sacking Jayden Daniels to bury Washington's comeback bid," Shook said. "The fashion in which this game ended might cause some to question the 49ers' standing atop the Power Rankings; we often fail to remember, however, that there are professional football players on both sides (and the Commanders feature a dynamic quarterback in Daniels).

"Kyle Shanahan's propensity for letting things get a little too close for comfort reared its unwelcome head again, but San Francisco finished the job like a proven winner usually does. Let's not allow the anxiety-inducing fourth quarter to overshadow how dominant the Niners were earlier in the game. They're undefeated and keeping the throne."

Behind the 49ers were the Chiefs, Bills, Vikings, and Jaguars. Complete unity here with ESPN's list with the exact same top five.

It was simple here for CBS's Pete Prisco, as the 49ers found a way to win again.

"They made it interesting against the Commanders, but they still found a way," Prisco wrote. "Now they face a long road trip to play the Falcons on a short week."

There was a slightly different top five here, as the Chiefs, Vikings, Bills, and Denver Broncos followed. The Broncos offense has been a big story, but they're 4-2 after facing one of the tougher schedules in the NFL to start the season.

The Niners remained at No. 1 here as well, with FOX Sports's Ralph Vacciano lauding the team's depth following the injuries, while pointing out they're clearly the best team in the NFL so far.

"The 49ers are held together at times by Band-Aids and gauze tape, but there's no question they're the best team in football a third of the way through the season," Vacciano wrote. "They need a rest, especially after WR Mike Evans reinjured his Achilles on Monday night, joining WR Deebo Samuel, WR Christian Kirk, edge rusher Nick Bosa and more on the sideline.

"But they're so deep and so good, they can sleepwalk through wins — like they seemed to do at times in the second half Monday night when they nearly blew their game against the Commanders. Now they just have to get through Atlanta to hit their bye week undefeated and see if they can get some of their walking wounded back after that.

The Niners will be favored again this week on the road against the Atlanta Falcons, giving them a chance to go 7-0 entering their bye week, where they can get healthier and acquire reinforcements through the trade market. So far, so good here for San Francisco.

articles.title: Mason McCormack chewed out Germie Bernard over fourth-down error
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormack held rookie Germie Bernard accountable after a key fourth-down mistake.
articles.body:
When a rookie wide receiver makes a mistake on fourth down, the response on the sideline often dictates how quickly they adapt to the speed and stakes of the NFL. For Pittsburgh Steelers rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard, a critical mistake during a key fourth-down sequence against Tampa Bay became an immediate lesson in accountability and situational awareness.

Catching an under route short of the line to gain, Bernard spotted a defender closing in on his upfield shoulder. Attempting to create space, he retreated to make the tackler miss, a habit that worked in college but proved costly in the pros. The defender brought Bernard down short of the line, turning the ball over on downs.

On a recent episode of his teammate Cameron Heyward's podcast, " Not Just Football with Cam Heyward ," Bernard detailed what happened. He said as he got up, guard Mason McCormick immediately let him hear it.

"McCormick, he's like, 'Sir, what the… are you doing? Get down. Go forward,'" Bernard recalled. "He's cussing me out and I'm like, 'Yeah, yeah. I need that. I need that.'"

Rather than wilting under the heated confrontation, Bernard embraced the tough love from his offensive lineman. The rookie recognized that high-stakes moments require brutal honesty, especially when individual instincts conflict with team goals.

Shortly after, head coach Mike McCarthy sat down with Bernard on the bench to reinforce the operational lesson behind McCormick's frustration.

"Coach came and sat down next to me. He was like, 'You just got to understand situational awareness,'" Bernard shared. "'First, second down, okay you can do that, but third, fourth down, you just got to catch it and fall forward. Don't try to do too much. Let the big plays come to you.'"

The sequence highlighted a crucial rite of passage for Pittsburgh's young core. Armed with direct accountability from McCormick and clear situational coaching from McCarthy and he bounced back later in the contest to score his first career NFL touchdown, proving that embracing sideline criticism is often the fastest path to rookie growth.

articles.title: Bills have another player suspended by NFL for a spitting incident vs. Raiders
articles.summary: This is now the second DB on the Bills to be suspended for spitting this week.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are coming off a big Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders and will now get a bye week to rest before returning to action in Week 8.

But for that Week 8 matchup, the Bills are going to be without a key defensive back, and not due to injury. Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was suspended by the NFL for a spitting incident during the Bills vs. Raiders game.

Somehow, he's not the only Bills DB to face this suspension from the NFL. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. is joining Gardner-Johnson on suspension for spitting in the Raiders game.

A second Bills DB suspended for spitting incident vs. Raiders

"Bills DB Sam Franklin Jr. was suspended one game today for unsportsmanlike conduct that the league said was a spitting incident vs. the Las Vegas Raiders," Schefter reports.

Franklin and Gardner-Johnson are two defensive backs now set to be suspended for the Bills' Week 8 game coming out of their Week 7 bye.

When the Bills face the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, they're going to be down a few defensive backs if these suspensions from the NFL hold up.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo is reporting that Franklin "denies the allegation" that he spit toward or on someone during the Raiders game. Franklin will appeal the suspension and try to avoid missing Week 8's matchup.

If both are out for that matchup, Buffalo will have to roll with Damar Hamlin, Jalon Kilgore, and Cole Bishop as their main safety rotation, as Gardner-Johnson and Franklin both might miss that game.

It's a wild situation for the Bills to find themselves in, as two defensive backs are now suspended for Week 8, barring an appeal changing things.

articles.title: Steve Young reveals HCs he’d most want to play for in today’s QB era
articles.summary: Decades before the dual-threat quarterback became all the rage in the NFL, Steve Young was doing it regularly. Casually, even. He would have fit right in wi...
articles.body:
Decades before the dual-threat quarterback became all the rage in the NFL, Steve Young was doing it regularly. Casually, even. He would have fit right in with today's game with his perfect mix of accuracy, speed, and mobility.

Young had a rocket arm, a sprinter's legs, and a knack for turning broken plays into magical highlights. When he retired in 1999 after a 15-year career, he was a three-time champion, a two-time MVP, a six-time All-Pro, and a seven-time Pro Bowler.

Young has kept tabs on the NFL , including the latest trends and modern strategies. On "The Pat McAfee Show," he revealed the current coaches he would like to play for.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I'd run down the street to play for Kyle (Shanahan). If I could go to Sean McVay, Sean Payton, and Andy Reid, I'd sprint to them," said Young.

"Those are the guys. Those are innovators. Those were the guys who were innovating back when the rules changed in 2018. They innovated, and now that people caught up with them, you know what they did? They innovated again and again. That's why I love them."

The 65-year-old icon added that he could see himself excelling in today's league , given his physical attributes and playing style.

"It's the era of the quarterback. It's like you've given all the rules to make them feel the power to be great," explained Young.

"This is my game, man! I wanna game like this. This is how I wanna roll. Drop back, rip it, be efficient, beat a man, and just start running around, eating up yards. Oh, it's a good game right now for quarterbacks."

He starred for the Los Angeles Express, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the San Francisco 49ers, amassing a 94-49 record.

Young would not need to reinvent his game to succeed in today's NFL. If anything, modern schemes might make his job easier. After all, for the legendary quarterback, it does not really matter what era it is.

articles.title: Jaguars Reacts Survey: Will Jacksonville win the AFC South this season?
articles.summary: Do you trust the Jaguars to protect their two-game lead in the division?
articles.body:
Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country.

The Jacksonville Jaguars just can't seem to get past the Houston Texans.

The Jags have a 13-3 record in their last 16 regular season games, but two of those three losses came against the Texans, including Sunday's 31-34 stunner .

"That was not the result that you hunt up each week," head coach Liam Coen said Monday.

"You never want to lose, but I am glad that we're able to respond in terms of the mental toughness of the group when it's not perfect or everything's not going exactly according to plan, and they just keep playing their tails off."

The Week 6 loss to Houston was a bummer, as was Jacksonville's 10-point blown lead to Denver in Week 2. At the end of the day, though, the Jaguars have a 4-2 record going into their bye. They lead the AFC South by two games over the Texans (2-4), Indianapolis Colts (2-4), and Tennessee Titans (1-5). And it's not fraudulent at all.

The top four teams in point differential this year are the Jaguars (+50) and the three remaining undefeated teams: the San Francisco 49ers (+67), Kansas City Chiefs (+57), and Minnesota Vikings (+45).

Jacksonville has performed like one of the best teams in the NFL — despite facing the league's seventh-toughest schedule so far this season, per Sharp Football Analysis . They're projected to have the single easiest schedule the rest of the way.

"To be six weeks in and to feel confident that your team's going to respond, that we're made of the right stuff to respond, and we have so much football left that you're excited about," Coen said.

"You're excited about getting things corrected; you're excited about being able to be in those moments again and maybe do it right or do it better the next time, as much as it hurts in the moment, in the aftermath. But I have a lot of confidence in this football team. Trevor [Lawrence] gives me so much confidence on a weekly basis as a play caller and the way that I think he's seeing it right now and playing. I'm very excited about this football team."

Did the latest loss to Houston make you worried about Jacksonville's lead in the division? Or do you feel comfortable predicting them to win the AFC South for a second straight season?

Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

articles.title: Keys for the Vikings' defense in Week 7 against the Colts
articles.summary: The Vikings' defense is set to make an impact in Week 7 against the Colts.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings enjoyed their Bye Week while the rest of the NFL dueled it out on the field in Week 6. They come into Week 7 recharged and ready to take on the Indianapolis Colts , who are dealing with some chaos of their own.

For the Vikings, though, they will be looking to set the tone early with their defense getting pressure on their former quarterback, Daniel Jones. On offense, all eyes will be on Kyler Murray, who hopes to build off what was a strong Week 5. He will have some extra attention after former Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy looked strong in his debut with the Giants . The Vikings will be focused on themselves, though, and making an example of the Colts.

In this preview piece, we will be discussing the keys on defense for Minnesota as they face an underwhelming Colts' offense.

This sounds silly when discussing a Brian Flores defense, but in Week 7 it will make or break this game. Daniel Jones needs to have a clean pocket to create and let his receivers get open; they need Jonathan Taylor to have time to read the defense; they cannot afford that time in Week 7. If Brian Flores comes out of the gate firing everything he has got, then this could be a fun game for his unit and the Vikings as a whole.

Jonathan Taylor is one of the bright spots of the entire Colts roster, not just the offense. He is sixth in the NFL in rushing yards this year with 492 yards and has found the endzone seven times in six games. The Colts will lean on him to control time of possession and to lead this offense, and it will be on the Vikings to contain him. If they can't, then this could be a long day for the Vikings' defense, as they haven't had one this season.

The Vikings know Daniel Jones from their one season together, and there is a lot of film on him. He cannot find success when a defense is creating chaos for him. Brian Flores and the Vikings can force a lot of turnovers by not allowing him time to process things. Whether it is from being reckless with the ball or making errant passes, he is turnover-prone. The Vikings need to capitalize on that in Week 7, and if they do, they can improve to 6-0.
